RagShortTexts: Baptism creates religious identity and ties to godparents.
Baptismal and everyday names can coexist.

Variants.Content: At baptism a priest receives the child into the Church through prayer and naming. Godparents witness and undertake religious care. Everyday and baptismal names may coexist; marriage arrangements also require attention to spiritual kinship.
Companions may use a household name but give a baptismal name to a priest. Godparenthood entails care, not a drinking oath entitling someone to military aid.
Powerful households gain connections through godparents, but spiritual kinship also constrains marriage. Checking relationships before exchanging gifts prevents disputes after a match is arranged.
Baptizing a child requires a priest and godparents whom relatives trust to provide care. Familiar names persist; the child needs identifiable people, not simply an impressive sponsor.
